stem:
Heena wants to find North using familiar star patterns. She knows the Big Dipper, the Little Dipper, and the Pole Star. She also notices the brightest star tonight.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The Pole Star is a member of the Big Dipper and slowly circles the sky each night.
The Pole Star belongs to the Little Dipper and appears nearly fixed, so it marks North.
The brightest star tonight must be the Pole Star and therefore marks North from any place on Earth.
The Big Dipper itself always sits due South, so it cannot help locate North.

teacher.key_rationale: The Pole Star is in the Little Dipper and stays nearly fixed in the North.
